Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: days of grace, your cash floor, the payment lag, retention, advance and interest rates and your warning days.
Fill Clients and Terms with the days each client has to pay and to certify and the interest rate for late payment. Claims, received, outstanding and a payer rating fill in.
Enter each contract on Project Billing with its value, retention and the share of work your site team measures every month. Billing against work done fills in.
Split every contract on Schedule of Values into the parts you claim against, then list the share done in each claim on Claim Lines.
Add a row on Progress Claims for each month. Work, variations, gross, retention, advance recovery, net, the due date and the status fill in; add variations on Variations in Claims.
Log each certificate on Payment Certificates and each payment on Client Payments. The cut, days late and late interest fill in, and the claim shows what is still owed.
Read Receivables Ageing every week, log calls on Overdue Follow-up and record disputes on Disputed Amounts.
Track Retention Held, Retention Released and Advance Payments for each contract; the balances and release dates fill in.
Enter supplier and subcontractor invoices on Payables and the weekly bank balance on Bank Balance Log, then plan the next 12 months on Cash Flow Forecast.
Keep Bonds and Guarantees, Final Accounts and Late Interest up to date so that nothing ends or goes unbilled.

Use the 14 calculators for the claim, retention, advance recovery, cash position, under and over billing, days to be paid, late interest, final account, cash gap, certificate check, bond expiry, billing curve and claim dates.
Read Cash Dashboard and Charts every week: money owed, overdue claims, retention, billing against work done, disputes and the months below your cash floor.
Run site safety, quality checks, snag lists and handover in one workbook
Control site safety, quality, snags and handover
Weekly site inspections with a pass mark
items checked and failed give a pass rate for each visit, a result against your own pass mark and a warning for any site that has not been inspected in time
every incident and near miss shows if it is recordable, how long it has been open and feeds the incident rate per 200,000 hours worked
hot work, height, excavation and other permits show their expiry and flag any permit left open after it ended
Risk score from likelihood and severity
likelihood times severity gives a score and a level for each risk assessment and method statement, with the date the review is due
each worker's certificates show the expiry date and a warning before they end, so nobody works on a task without a valid course
actions from inspections, incidents and audits show due date, days late and owner, with a message ready to send
Concrete cube results checked against the grade
strength at 7 and 28 days is compared with the strength required, so a weak result is seen the day it is crushed
each report records the trade, severity and cost of the rework and turns overdue if it stays open too long
Snag list for hundreds of items
every snag has a location, trade, subcontractor and due date, and the closure forecast shows the date the list will be empty
manuals, drawings, certificates, warranties and the safety file are tracked for each project with their due date and days late
defects show days open and repair cost, and each warranty shows its expiry so a claim is made before the cover ends

One row for each project; inspections, last inspection, incidents, open actions, open snags and an inspection status fill in from the other sheets.
Hours worked on each site by month
One row for each site and month with the hours worked by everyone on site; the incident rate uses these hours.
One row for each inspection with the items checked and failed; pass rate, result against your pass mark, month and the supervisor phone fill in.
One row for each incident or near miss with its kind, cause, severity and lost days; recordable, status, days open, month and the manager phone fill in.
One row for each short safety talk with its topic, who led it and how many attended; month and the site name fill in.
Permits to work: hot work, height, excavation and more
One row for each permit with its kind, area, days valid and when it was closed; expiry, days left and a status that shows permits left open fill in.
One row for each risk assessment or method statement with likelihood and severity from 1 to 5; score, level, next review date and review status fill in.
One row for each issue of protective equipment with its quantity, cost and life in days; the cost, the replacement date and a replacement status fill in.
Safety observations from walks around the site
One row for each safe act, unsafe act, unsafe condition or good practice noticed; month, the site name and a positive flag fill in.
Corrective actions from inspections, incidents and audits
One row for each action with its source, due date and owner; status, days late, month and the supervisor phone fill in.
Safety training matrix: who holds which certificate
One row for each certificate a worker holds with the date done and the months it stays valid; expiry date, days left and status fill in.
Emergency drills and how fast the site responded
One row for each drill with the minutes taken against the target; the result, month and the site name fill in.
Quality inspections and test plan checks
One row for each inspection of a trade item with its result; the pass or fail flag, month and the site name fill in.
One row for each cube crushed with the grade, age and strength; the strength required at that age, the margin and the result fill in.
Non-conformance reports and the cost of rework
One row for each non-conformance with its trade, severity and cost; status, days open and month fill in, and old ones turn overdue.
One row for each snag item with its location, trade and subcontractor; due date, status, days open, month and the subcontractor phone fill in.
Handover documents checklist for each project
One row for each document the client must receive with its due date and when it arrived; status and days late fill in.
Defects reported during the defects period
One row for each defect with its trade, cause and repair cost; status, days open, month and the subcontractor phone fill in.
One row for each warranty with the supplier, start date and years; expiry date, days left and status fill in so no claim is missed.
Client satisfaction scores at handover and after
One row for each client survey with five scores from 1 to 5; the average, month and the band against your target fill in.

Hello, the last safety inspection at "{name}" was {days_since} days ago. Please inspect the site today and send the result.
Send a weekly safety message to a site
Hello, please hold the weekly toolbox talk at "{name}" this week and send the attendance. There are {open_actions} open actions on your site.
Ask for actions after a fail
Hello, the inspection of "{site}" on {date} found {failed} failed items: {finding}. Please send your actions today.
Thank a site for a good inspection
Hello, the inspection of "{site}" on {date} passed with {pass_rate}. Thank you to the whole crew for keeping the site safe.
Hello, the incident at "{site}" on {date} ({summary}) is still {state}. Please send the statements and the root cause.
Share the lesson from an incident
Hello, please share the lesson from the incident at "{site}" on {date} at the next toolbox talk: {summary}.
Warn that a permit is ending
Hello, the permit {pt_id} at "{site}" ends on {expires}. Close it, or ask for a new one before more work.
Ask to close an expired permit
Hello, the permit {pt_id} at "{site}" expired on {expires} and is not closed. Please check the area and close it today.
Ask for a risk document review
Hello, the document for "{activity}" at "{site}" is due for review on {next_review}. Please review it with the crew.
Remind an owner of an action
Hello, the action "{what}" at "{site}" is due on {due}. Please finish it and tell us.
Hello, the action "{what}" at "{site}" is {days_late} days late. Please tell us today when it will be done.
Thank an owner for closing an action
Hello, thank you for closing "{what}" at "{site}". The site is safer because of it.
Warn a worker that a certificate ends
Hello {worker}, your {course} certificate ends on {expires}. Please book a refresher before then.
Tell a worker a certificate ended
Hello {worker}, your {course} certificate ended on {expires}. You cannot do that task until you renew it.
Hello {worker}, we booked a place for you on the {course} course. Please confirm that you can attend.
Hello, we raised report {nc_id} at "{site}": {issue}. Please send your correction plan within 5 days.
Hello, report {nc_id} at "{site}" has been open for {days_open} days. Please correct the work and tell us.
Send a snag to a subcontractor
Hello, please fix this at "{site}": {item} in {location}. We ask you to finish by {due}.
Hello, the snag "{item}" at "{site}" is {days_open} days old and late. Please come this week to fix it.
Ask to confirm a snag is fixed
Hello, please confirm that "{item}" at "{site}" in {location} is fixed, so that we can check it and close the item.
Hello, we still need the handover document "{doc}" for "{site}", due on {due}. Please send it this week.
Hello, the handover document "{doc}" for "{site}" is {days_late} days late. The handover cannot finish without it.
Hello, we received "{doc}" for "{site}". Thank you.
Send a defect to a subcontractor
Hello, a defect was reported at "{site}": {what}. Please attend this week and tell us when you can come.
Hello, the defect "{what}" at "{site}" has been open for {days_open} days. The client is waiting. Please repair it now.
Ask a subcontractor to confirm a repair
Hello, please confirm that the repair of "{what}" at "{site}" is finished so that we can tell the client.
Ask a supplier about a warranty claim
Hello, we have a fault on "{item}" at "{site}", under your warranty until {expires}. Please tell us how to make the claim.
Hello, please confirm that the warranty on "{item}" at "{site}" ends on {expires} and send the certificate.

This permit allows the described work from {col:permits.issued} until {col:permits.expires}. The work must follow the method statement, and the supervisor must check the area before work starts and after it ends.
Everyone on the job must know the hazards, the emergency plan and the point to stop work. Close the permit when the work is finished.
Person in charge of the work
Site: {col:incidents.site}. Date of the incident: {col:incidents.date}. Kind: {col:incidents.kind}.
We report the following: {col:incidents.summary}. The likely cause is recorded as {col:incidents.cause}. The number of days lost so far is {col:incidents.lost_days}.
We are investigating and will send you the findings and the actions to stop it happening again.
The following action is required: {col:actions.what}. It was opened on {col:actions.opened} and it is due on {col:actions.due}.
Please confirm in writing when the action is done, so that the supervisor can check it on site.
We found the following work that does not meet the specification: {col:ncr.issue}. It was raised on {col:ncr.raised}.
Please send your plan to correct the work and the date you will finish. The estimated cost of the rework is {col:ncr.cost}, and we may recover it as the contract allows.
The worker completed this course on {col:training.done}. The certificate stays valid for {col:training.valid_months} months and ends on {col:training.expires}.
The worker must refresh the course before the end date to keep working on tasks that need it.
We hand over the works to the client. The handover pack contains the manuals, drawings, certificates, warranties and training records listed in the handover sheet.
Open snag items at the date of this certificate: {col:projects.open_snags}. We will finish them as agreed, and the defects period starts from this date.
A defect was reported during the defects period: {col:defects.what}. The probable cause is {col:defects.dcause}.
Please repair it within {set:defect_days} days of this notice. The estimated cost is {col:defects.cost}. Tell us when you can attend so that we can arrange access.
Warranty handover letter to the client
The warranty on this item starts on {col:warr.start}, lasts {col:warr.years} years and ends on {col:warr.expires}.
Please keep this letter with your records and contact the supplier on {col:warr.phone} if you find a fault. We will help you make a claim.
We found the following item that needs to be put right: {col:snags.item}. It was raised on {col:snags.raised}, and we ask you to finish it by {col:snags.due}.
Please tell us when it is done so that we can check it and close the item.
Thank you and survey follow-up for a client
Thank you for sharing your opinion on our work. Your average score is {col:sat.avg} out of 5, and your comment was: {col:sat.comment}.
We use every answer to improve our safety, quality and communication, and we will contact you if you asked for a follow-up.

Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: days between inspections, pass mark, risk scores, warning days and the share of the grade expected at 7 days.
Fill Sites with each project, its manager, supervisor and phones. Inspections, incidents, open actions and open snags fill in from the other sheets.
Add the hours worked on each site every month on Site Hours. The incident rate per 200,000 hours uses them.
Record each weekly walk on Site Inspections with the items checked and failed. The pass rate and result fill in, and a site that is not inspected in time turns red.
Log every incident and near miss on Incidents. Recordable, days open and status fill in, and the cause and kind feed the charts.
Issue permits on Permits to Work and keep Risk and Method Register up to date. Expired permits and reviews that are due show at once.
Keep Training Matrix, PPE Issued, Toolbox Talks, Safety Observations and Emergency Drills current. Certificates and PPE show their end date.
Send every finding to Corrective Actions with an owner and a due date, then read the days late each week.
For quality, use Quality Inspections, Concrete Tests and Non-conformance Reports. Cubes are compared with the strength required and old reports turn overdue.
Near the end of a project, list snag items on Snag List and handover documents on Handover Documents. After handover, record Defects and Warranties and the client score on Client Satisfaction.

Use the 14 calculators for incident rate, days without incident, site score, risk rating, snag forecast, defect cost, concrete strength, PPE reorder, training expiry, handover readiness and warranties.
Print 10 sheets and 10 letters, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Safety and Quality Dashboard and Charts every week: incidents, inspections, permits, actions, certificates, snags and handover.
